heading: Rajasthan Municipal Election Result 2026 Live Updates: Chairperson elections in 305 urban bodies to be held on September 21-22
paragraphs: Rajasthan Election Result 2026 Live Updates: The Bharatiya Janata Party has emerged ahead of the Congress in Rajasthan’s urban local body elections, but the contest was far closer than the BJP’s wins in some of the state’s major cities might suggest. Across 309 civic bodies, the BJP polled 35.18 per cent of the total votes, compared with 34.24 per cent for the Congress, giving it a lead of just 0.94 percentage points, or 99,615 votes. Independent candidates also made a significant mark, accounting for 27.38 per cent of the vote, while the None of the Above option polled more votes than several regional and national parties.

In Jaipur, the BJP secured control of the Municipal Corporation board after winning 78 of the 146 wards for which results have been declared. The Congress won 53 wards, while Independents bagged 15. The results in the remaining four wards will be decided after repolling at five booths, where electronic voting machine results could not be retrieved because of technical issues. Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the BJP’s performance, saying the mandate reflected support for the party’s policies of good governance and development under the “double-engine” government.

The BJP’s victory was even more decisive in Udaipur, where it won 53 of the 80 wards and secured an absolute majority in the Municipal Corporation board for the seventh consecutive term. The Congress was a distant second with 23 seats. A BJP candidate credited the victory to collective effort and the leadership of Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma, state BJP president Madan Rathore and the city’s two MLAs.

Last election: Jaipur had two municipal corporations in the 2020 election, with the Congress and BJP winning one each. The polls covered 250 wards across the Heritage and Greater corporations, with an average voter turnout of 57.5%. This time, Jaipur went to polls for 150 wards

Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati on Tuesday claimed that several BSP candidates were "forcibly defeated" during recounts by razor-thin margins due to irregularities involving government machinery. She noted that without such interference, the party would have recorded an even stronger performance across the state's local bodies.
In an X post, Mayawati extended congratulatory greetings to party workers on Tuesday after the BSP secured 19 councillor seats in the Rajasthan municipal elections.

"In the municipal elections held in Rajasthan, the BSP has also succeeded this time by getting its councillors elected to 19 seats, and many candidates were forcibly defeated in the recount by a margin of just a few votes due to irregularities in the government machinery; otherwise, the party could have achieved an even better result here. For this, the party has extended hearty congratulations and best wishes to all the small and big office-bearers and workers of the BSP," she said.

https://twitter.com/Mayawati/status/2099692837407502578 The remarks came after the Bharatiya Janata Party secured a resounding victory in the Rajasthan urban local body elections, winning the Jaipur Municipal Corporation board with 78 seats, while independent candidates have emerged as key players in several other civic bodies where no party has secured a clear majority. ANI

The State Election Commission on Tuesday issued the public notice for the election of chairpersons in 305 urban local bodies across Rajasthan. The elections, excluding the municipal corporations of Jaipur, Jodhpur and Kota and the Suket municipality, will be held on September 21 and 22, as per the previously announced schedule.

Re-polling will be held on September 16 at 10 polling booths across four urban local bodies where the chairperson elections had been postponed. The votes will be counted on September 17, following which the public notice for the chairperson elections in these four bodies will be issued.

In Jaipur, the final results in four wards of the Municipal Corporation are still pending after technical issues with electronic voting machines. Re-polling will be held at five booths in Wards 9, 18, 25 and 34. Jaipur District Collector Sandesh Nayak said results could not be retrieved from the machines at the affected booths.

Meanwhile, counting has been completed in eight of Rajasthan’s 10 municipal corporations. The BJP is set to form boards in Jaipur, Kota, Udaipur and Bhilwara, while the Congress has secured a clear majority in the Bikaner Municipal Corporation.
Telangana BJP president Ramchander Rao said the BJP’s performance in Rajasthan’s urban local body elections was an indicator of the public mood across the country.

Rao alleged that the Congress and the INDIA bloc had attempted to defame the BJP government in Rajasthan and spread “propaganda” against the party. He said the election results had delivered a clear message, adding that the BJP remained ahead through the polls and thanking the people of Rajasthan for supporting the party.

The BJP polled 37,35,567 votes, compared with the Congress’s 36,35,952, giving the BJP a lead of 99,615 votes, or 0.94 per cent. Independent candidates accounted for a significant 27.38 per cent of the vote, with 29,06,787 votes, while NOTA received 1.03 per cent, or 1,09,523 votes.
The BJP won 78 seats in the Jaipur Municipal Corporation board. Independents also emerged as key players in several civic bodies where no party secured a clear majority.

The Bharatiya Janata Party registered a decisive victory in the Udaipur Municipal Corporation elections, winning 53 of the 80 wards and securing an absolute majority for the seventh consecutive term. The Congress finished a distant second with 23 seats.

A BJP winner credited the victory to the party’s collective effort and the leadership of the state unit. Following the results, he highlighted the role of Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma, state president Madan Rathore and the two local MLAs in the party’s success.

The Rajasthan urban local body election results have given the BJP a clear edge, though not an overwhelming mandate. Across 309 municipal bodies covering 10,244 wards, the BJP has won 4,166 seats, compared with 3,595 for the Congress — a margin of 571 seats. The BJP has secured an outright majority in 85 civic bodies and emerged as the single-largest party in another 60, giving it the lead in 145 of the 309 Urban Local Bodies. The Congress, meanwhile, has won a majority in 46 bodies and emerged as the largest party in another 54, putting it ahead in 100 Urban Local Bodies.
The Bharatiya Janata Party secured victory in Udaipur, winning 53 wards out of a total of 80 wards. Congress could secure victory in 23 wards.

BJP leads in Alwar with 28 seats currently, while Congress is ahead with 23 seats. Bahujan Samaj Party leads with 1 seat. The Alwar Nagar Nigam has a total of 65 seats.
BJP leads in Ganganagar with 30 wards out of 65 seats. Congress leads with 17 seats, while independent candidates lead with 18 seats, as per the latest State Election Commission data.
Congress leads in Bikaner with 40 seats out of 80. BJP is at 27, as per the data by the State Election Commission
BJP is ahead in Jaisalmer with 25 wards while Congress stands at 16.
In Kota Nagar Nigam polls, BJP has taken the lead with 30 seats out of a total of 100 seats. Congress, on the other hand, could secure 20 seats as the counting proceeds.

Congress wins Ajmer with 37 wards, while the BJP could secure 32. In Bikaner, Congress leads with 15 wards while the BJP has 10 as counting progresses. BJP leads in Jaipur and Udaipur as per the latest poll data released by the State Election Commission.

The CPI(M) is set to form the board in Nokha Nagar Palika after winning 29 of the 45 wards, with the BJP securing 13 and Independents three. The result comes as a boost for the Left party, which has positioned itself as an alternative to the BJP in the absence of a strong Congress presence in the municipality. CPI(M) state secretary Kishan Parikh attributed the victory to local issues and voter dissatisfaction with the BJP, saying the party had emerged as an alternative on economic and civic concerns. Across the state, the CPI(M) fielded 192 candidates and around 40 won their wards. The party had also made a surprise electoral gain in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, when Amra Ram won the Sikar seat as an INDIA bloc candidate.
The BJP is leading in Jaipur and Udaipur. Congress is currently leading in Jodhpur Nagar Nigam, Ajmer.

The BJP has retained control over the civic body elections, the results of which were announced on Monday. The saffron camp was leading in key urban bodies, including Jaipur, Udaipur and Ajmer. Congress was leading in Jodhpur Nagar Nigam.

The BJP is currently leading in Jaipur, Udaipur and Kota as results for the urban local body elections continue to come in, while the Congress is ahead in Jodhpur and Pali Nagar Nigam. Pali is the home turf of state BJP chief Madan Rathore.

Congress Legislature Party chief whip Rafiq Khan said the early results in the Jaipur Municipal Corporation polls favour the BJP because several Congress seats are yet to be declared. Claiming that Congress would gain in the remaining rounds, Khan said, " The counting for those hasn't even been done yet... For example, if you talk about my assembly constituency, we will win 2-3 more seats than the BJP... However, the 4-5 seats that have been declared are for the BJP. Our seats are yet to be declared. We will win 8-10 seats. The results for those are still awaited. A similar trend is happening in Kishanpole and Hawamahal... our score will go up to 60+..."

The BJP is leading across several urban local bodies in Rajasthan as counting continues. In the 47 Nagar Parishads, the BJP is ahead in 18, while the Congress leads in 5 and Independents in two. In Nagar Palikas, the BJP is leading in 139 local bodies, compared with 98 for the Congress and 9 for Independents. The figures shows the party leading in each local body as a whole.

The BJP is leading in 9 municipal corporations across Rajasthan, including Jaipur, Udaipur, Jodhpur, Pali, Bhilwara, Kota, Alwar, Ajmer and Bikaner, as counting of votes continues for the urban local body elections.

Results have started coming in from the Rajasthan urban local body elections. Early trends from Jaipur show the BJP and Congress taking the lead in several wards with BJP candidates Neeraj Agarwal (Ward 121) and Vijay Agarwal (Ward 31) have won, while Congress candidates Rakesh Lata (Ward 21) and Durgesh Sharma (Ward 101) have also won.

More than 61.93 lakh voters cast their ballots amid reports of minor clashes, EVM glitches and allegations of bogus voting in several areas. The Congress also alleged that a party worker in Pali died following poll-related harassment by BJP workers, while another person in Sikar was allegedly killed by a BJP candidate’s vehicle. The party has sought investigations into both incidents.
The second phase of polling ended on Friday, with 70.68% voter turnout amid reports of clashes, EVM glitches and allegations of bogus voting.

Counting of votes is underway across 10,167 wards in 309 urban local bodies in Rajasthan. In Jaipur, the counting is being held ward-wise across 15 rooms with 150 tables, covering wards in Vidhyadhar Nagar, Jhotwara, Sanganer, Bagru, Malviya Nagar, Civil Lines, Kishanpole, Adarsh Nagar, Hawa Mahal and Amer. Counting for two municipal councils and 16 municipalities in Jaipur district is also being conducted at designated centres.
